hypotheses.statement: Customers experience dissatisfaction mainly because they lack visibility into existing, reliable shipment data; surfacing DA-ORD, DA-WMS and DA-PICK data via a chatbot will resolve the 'why is my parcel late' problem.

hypotheses.statement: Lateness is actually caused by operational friction in pickup scheduling, since pickup schedule changes require carrier (SH-CAR) human approval (K-SCHED), producing real delays rather than a communication deficit.

hypotheses.statement: Parcels are late because of upstream warehouse job processing delays (tracked in DA-WMS) before they ever reach the carrier handoff.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): the stakeholder request (CL-01, SH-CX) was for a chatbot explaining why parcels are late, framed as a communication/visibility gap, but the root problem established is that 30% of 1000 orders are late at the handover stage (E-02) primarily because the WMS RELEASE-BATCH job fails in 21 of 30 runs, releasing 290 orders to the carrier only after pickup already occurred (E-04).

The logistics lead's claim that the carrier's 2-hour pickup delay (E-03, matching the measured E-01/E-06 median of 2.0h) is the root cause was tested and contradicted by the authoritative wms-jobs evidence E-04; this is tracked as open conflicts C-1 and C-2.

Hypothesis testing: H-COMMUNICATION-GAP (chatbot alone fixes it) and H-CARRIER-SCHEDULE-FRICTION (carrier scheduling friction is the cause) were REJECTED; H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESS-DELAY and H-HANDOFF-DATA-GAP were SUPPORTED, pointing to warehouse batch failure plus an unreliable Shop→Carrier handoff (H-PICK, unknown delivery_status/semantic_validity) as the real drivers.

DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS: the handoff validity check and two critical unknowns (U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY) were deferred to verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved.

What was released: the solution design's release_scope and minimum_useful_scope cover only correlate_pickup_and_release_timestamps:DA-PICK, delivered via work item W-WI-01-PICKUP-SLOT-CORRELATIO (status DONE, using the pickup-log pickup_by_slot query, E-06).

The design explicitly declines to use the only available protected/write action (push_pickup_schedule) as a remedy (SR-NO-PICKUP-SCHEDULE-PUSH), since authoritative evidence E-04 contradicts carrier delay as primary cause and H-CARRIER-SCHEDULE-FRICTION was rejected; the chatbot build itself (CL-01) is formally deferred (SR-DEFER-CHATBOT-SCOPE) until failure-rate success criteria are met.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no holds. This reflects that the diagnostic/correlation scope delivered is backed by complete, authoritative pickup-log data (E-01, E-06), while the broader root-cause and data-completeness questions remain open outside release scope (VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, VOB-U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY, VOB-R-3).
limitations_explained: Completeness of DA-ORD and DA-WMS is UNKNOWN (data_assets), so the measured 30% handover-late rate (E-02) and 70% RELEASE-BATCH failure rate (E-04) may be imprecise; note the released limitation text also lists DA-PICK as UNKNOWN completeness, though the data_assets record shows DA-PICK completeness as COMPLETE – this inconsistency is reported as-is from the input.

The underlying cause of the RELEASE-BATCH job's 70% failure rate (VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE) and the data-completeness validity question (VOB-U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY) remain OPEN and are outside the current release's blocking_scope, meaning intended_scope items diagnose_release_batch_failure:DA-WMS and audit_data_completeness:DA-ORD were not resolved.

The Shop→Carrier handoff H-PICK still has UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity and cannot be instrumented in this release, so no system holds a reliable 'reason for lateness' record for any future customer-facing explanation.

Unknown U-CARRIER-VS-WAREHOUSE-SEPARAT (MEDIUM, OPEN) – whether a compounding carrier-side delay exists on top of the warehouse batch issue – can only be partially addressed because both DA-PICK and DA-WMS (the two correlated data assets) carry unresolved completeness questions.

VOB-R-3 (impact HIGH, OPEN) questions whether the DA-PICK/DA-WMS correlation reliably resolves the independent-carrier-delay question given UNKNOWN completeness, and its blocking_scope (surface_lateness_reason:SH-CX, diagnose_release_batch_failure:DA-WMS) sits outside what was actually released.
proposal.summary: The customer-experience stakeholder (SH-CX) asked for a chatbot to tell customers why their parcel is late (CL-01). Investigation (PD-1) established the root problem differently from the initial framing and from logistics lead SH-LOG's claim that a 2-hour carrier pickup delay (E-03) was the cause: authoritative wms-jobs evidence (E-04) shows the warehouse RELEASE-BATCH job failed in 21 of 30 runs, releasing 290 orders to the carrier only after pickup had already happened, and order-db (E-02) shows 30% of 1000 orders are flagged late at the handover stage. The carrier-delay hypothesis (H-CARRIER-SCHEDULE-FRICTION) and the pure-visibility hypothesis (H-COMMUNICATION-GAP, i.e. 'just build the chatbot') were both REJECTED; warehouse-process-delay and handoff-data-gap hypotheses were SUPPORTED. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the critical open questions about the RELEASE-BATCH root cause and overall data completeness as verification obligations (VOBs). What was actually released is narrow: only the pickup-vs-release timestamp correlation on DA-PICK (work item W-WI-01, done via the pickup-log pickup_by_slot query, E-06), matching the solution design's minimum_useful_scope and release_scope. The design deliberately avoided pushing a pickup-schedule change (the one available write action) since the evidence contradicts carrier delay as root cause, and deferred the chatbot build itself until failure-rate targets are met. The final decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, because the delivered correlation work rests on complete, authoritative pickup data while several higher-impact root-cause and data-quality questions (tracked as open VOBs: VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, VOB-U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY, VOB-R-3) remain unresolved and are explicitly outside this release's scope.
